entries.title: Jump to the brand kit from any surface it drives
entries.summary: A palette icon now appears next to every design surface that reads from a **Brand kit** — the event page builder, system email designer, title slide designer (**Colours** panel, next to **Reset to brand**), clip export editor (**Renders**), and the Create carousel toolbar (when a kit is selected). Clicking the icon opens the exact kit the design uses in a new tab, so unsaved work in the editor is not lost. Hovering or focusing the icon shows a tooltip listing which kit assets — logo, colour swatches, fonts, tagline, hashtags or clip caption style — that surface actually pulls from.

where.path: Marketing → Brand / Slides / Clips / Create

entries.use_case: When an organizer notices a colour or font looks off in a slide, clip or email design, they can click the palette icon to jump straight to the brand kit driving that design — without hunting through menus — and fix the source asset in one step.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for all customers with Brand kit access (limited_release). No configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to keep slides, clips and emails visually consistent, or when they struggle to find which kit is driving a particular design.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers actively using Brand kits with Slides, Clips, or Create carousels.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Brand → any kit; or open a slide/clip/carousel/page-builder design and look for the palette icon
internal.gotchas: The link is intentionally absent from booklets, Advocacy Quick Launch and Advocacy video templates — those surfaces do not read the Marketing brand kit, so the link would point at irrelevant assets. Webinar share cards and email signatures are also not yet wired (coming in a follow-up branch).
internal.talk_track: Every design surface that uses your brand kit now has a palette icon that takes you straight to that kit in a new tab — so you can check or update the source without losing your place in the editor.

draft.docs_gap: The brand-kits guide should add a section listing every surface that displays the palette shortcut icon and explaining that the tooltip shows which specific kit assets (logo, colours, fonts, voice, clips) that surface reads.
draft.why_use_it: Brand kits let you define your event's logo, colours, fonts, voice and content rules in one place so every marketing surface — slides, clips, carousels, page builder and system emails — stays visually consistent without manual updates. When a kit changes, every surface that reads from it reflects the update automatically. Use a brand kit whenever you want a team of contributors to produce on-brand content without coordinating design decisions individually.

entries.title: Create credits quotes to the person who said them
entries.summary: Drafts in **Create** now credit quotes and paraphrases to the participant tagged on that part of the transcript — "Name, Job Title, Company" by default — instead of "one speaker". Hover a citation to see who said it, their session role and the timestamp; citations from untagged parts of the transcript are flagged so you can tag the speaker and **Redraft**. **Settings → Speaker credit** chooses the format, and **Copilot** can answer "who said this?" and fix attributions using the same data.

where.path: Marketing → Create → a project → Settings → Speaker credit

entries.use_case: When a marketer drafts a one-pager or blog from a session, the quotes come out credited to the real speaker — name, title and company — instead of "one panelist said", so the draft is ready to publish without a round of copy-pasting speaker details.

cs_action.note: On for every Create user. Attribution follows the transcript speaker tags, so a draft is only as good as the tagging.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer complains that Create drafts say "a speaker" or that Copilot asks them to paste a speaker's name (SB-10990).
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Live Transcribe or Media transcripts with Create.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Create → open a project with a tagged session in Sources → Redraft, then hover a citation
internal.gotchas: Untagged transcript passages stay generic by design. Participants whose seat on the session is hidden are never named. Old drafts keep their old citations until Redraft.
internal.talk_track: Create now knows who said what. Tag speakers in the transcript once and every draft credits them by name, title and company.

entries.title: Report a subsession's parent session fields on the same row
entries.summary: The Report Builder has a **Parent session** group of fields, labelled **Parent Session …** so their columns are easy to tell apart. On a subsession row it adds the session's own values — **Format**, **Track**, **Level**, **Language**, **Room**, **Status**, **Submitter**, **Title**, **Description**, its other standard fields and its custom fields — next to the subsession and its participants. Each subsession has one parent, so the report gains no extra rows, and you can filter and sort on these fields. Before, a subsession row only showed the session's title and IDs; its Format, Track and custom fields came from the subsession itself, which is usually blank.

where.path: Reports → Report Builder → Fields → Parent session

entries.use_case: A program team that collects presentations as subsessions needs one roster with the session's format, track, submitter and description next to every presenter — for a program book, a disclosure review or a CME export — without matching two spreadsheets on Session ID.

cs_action.note: ASA (ANESTHESIOLOGY 2027 / ADVANCE 2028) asked for this (HubSpot ticket 50511758943, SB-11095); build or update their subsession submission report with the Parent session fields. Any customer using subsessions with format/track on the parent benefits.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports blank Format or Track columns on a subsession report, duplicate rows on a session report with subsession columns, or exports two reports to match in Excel.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who collect presentations, abstracts or talks as subsessions under a parent session (medical and scientific meetings especially).
internal.staff_path: Event → Reports → open or create a Sessions report → Fields → Parent session
internal.gotchas: Parent session fields are empty on a session's own row — filter Is Subsession is Yes. Restricted (record-scoped) team roles can use the fields on a Sessions report but cannot pick Parent session as the report's main subject.
internal.talk_track: Subsession reports can now carry the session's format, track, submitter, description and custom fields on every row, so one report replaces matching two exports.

entries.title: Report Builder shows descriptions and other rich text as readable text
entries.summary:
Rich-text fields — session **Description**, speaker **Biography**, group and task descriptions, and custom **Rich Text** or **Text Area** fields — now come back as readable text in the Report Builder preview and in CSV and Excel downloads, instead of editor HTML like `

…

`. Paragraphs, line breaks and list items stay on separate lines; filters still match the text as stored. Dashboards, share links and Ask return the same text.

where.path: Reports → Report Builder

entries.use_case: An organizer exporting session descriptions for a program book or a CME submission gets clean text they can paste, without stripping HTML tags in Excel.

cs_action.note: Applies to every report automatically. ASA reported it (HubSpot 50511758943, SB-11086).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says descriptions or bios in a report or export are full of tags.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone who reports on descriptions, bios or rich-text custom fields.
internal.staff_path: Event → Reports → any Sessions report → add Description → preview or Download
internal.gotchas: Formatting (bold, links) is not kept — the export is plain text. Saved reports pick this up without changes.
internal.talk_track: Descriptions and bios now export as clean text, with paragraphs and list items on their own lines.

entries.title: Number fields keep leading zeros, such as member IDs
entries.summary: A **Number** field now keeps a value exactly as typed, so a member ID like **0755092** keeps its leading zero when it is edited on a contact, in a grid cell, in Bulk Edit, on a submission or portal form, or filled in from a membership lookup. Before, a new contact kept the zero but any later edit saved 755092. The contacts grid and reports show the ID as stored. Values still sort, filter and add up as numbers.

where.path: Contacts → contact profile / grid; forms

entries.use_case: Associations that store member or customer IDs with leading zeros in a Number field can match them to their CRM without the IDs changing on edit.

cs_action.note: ASA (SB-11093): 274 ASA IDs lost their zero before the fix; Josh runs the repair after ASA confirms IDs are 7 digits. Other orgs with leading-zero numbers in US: 7 (182 values), EU: 2 (383).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says IDs in a Number field lose a leading zero, or match inconsistently to their CRM.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers storing member, customer or NPI-style IDs in Number fields.
internal.staff_path: Event → Contacts → a contact → a Number custom field
internal.gotchas: Values that already lost the zero are not changed by the fix; they need a repair (retype, or a staff SQL fix). Opening a CSV directly in Excel still drops leading zeros (Excel does that) — use the Excel download. Still numeric, so still zero-less: the Public API returns Number values as numbers, and the legacy module exports and email merge tags print through the value-types package (parseFloat) until that package is released.
internal.talk_track: Number fields now keep IDs exactly as you type them, leading zeros included.

entries.title: Live Transcribe lists each session participant once
entries.summary: The **Participants** card on a session in the **Live Transcribe Console** lists each person once, under the session role they hold. Before, a participant with a custom role such as **Panelist** also appeared a second time as **Speaker**.

where.path: Live Transcribe Console → a session → Participants

entries.use_case: An AV crew or producer checking who is on stage sees the real panel line-up once, with each person's role, instead of a doubled list that looks like extra speakers.

cs_action.note: Automatic for every Live Transcribe event. Reported by Clarion / Infocast (SB-11085); prod had 18,442 sessions in 78 US events with the duplicate rows.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports a Panelist, Moderator or other custom-role participant listed twice, once as Speaker, in Live Transcribe.
internal.who_should_get_it: Live Transcribe customers whose sessions use custom participant roles (panels, moderated sessions).
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Transcribe → Invites → open the Console link → a session → Participants
internal.gotchas: Display fix only; the underlying participant data did not change.
internal.talk_track: The Participants card now shows the panel as it really is, one line per person under their role.

entries.title: Tagged speaker names show wherever a transcript is read
entries.summary: Once you tag a voice on a recording or Live Transcribe session, the person's name replaces the "Speaker 4" placeholder in transcript search results, **Ask** answers, chapters, session recaps and the **Attend** app's session recap. A generic tag such as "Audience Member 2" shows its label. A participant whose seat on the session is hidden is never named, and names that come from the recording platform (Zoom, Goldcast) are kept.

where.path: Marketing → Media → a recording → Speakers → Tag

entries.use_case: A marketing team that tags speakers once gets recaps, chapters and search results that credit the right person by name, without re-importing the recording or fixing names by hand.

cs_action.note: Automatic, read-time: existing tags apply immediately with no re-import (SB-10990, API side).

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says recaps, search results or Ask answers say "Speaker 4" even though the speakers were tagged.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Live Transcribe or Media with speaker tagging.
internal.staff_path: Event → Marketing → Media → a recording → Speakers → Tag; then search the transcript or regenerate a recap
internal.gotchas: Already-generated recaps and stored quotes keep the placeholder until regenerated / re-extracted; clip chat and home search do not resolve tags yet. Brand Voice examples also match tagged names now (limited release, not in the public summary). Create's speaker credit and citation tooltip are a separate entry (create-speaker-attribution) that needs web-ui-v2#1457 in production.
internal.talk_track: Tag a speaker once and their name follows the transcript everywhere it is used.

entries.title: Forms on a trial event show a Trial mode banner and don't take submissions
entries.summary: While an organization or event is on a trial, its public forms show a **Trial mode** banner. Submitters can fill in a form and **Save as draft**, but **Submit** and payment are off, on call for papers forms and on the event website's award, request, reviewer, registration and RSVP forms. Everything opens as soon as the trial ends.

where.path: Public call for papers forms and event website pages of a trial organization or event

entries.use_case: A team setting up its event before the contract is signed can build, share and test its forms without collecting real submissions or payments by accident.

cs_action.note: Trial is a staff flag on the org or event. Before a trial customer opens a call for papers, nominations or registration, staff must turn trial off for the org and the event, or every final submit and payment is refused (403 trial_mode). Drafts and admin previews still work.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When onboarding a customer on a trial, and whenever a customer reports "Trial mode" on a live form or that submitters can't press Submit or Pay.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations or events Sessionboard has put on a trial (pre-contract or pre-renewal).
internal.staff_path: Staff only: turn off trial on the organization and on the event; the banner and the block clear at once (nothing is cached).
internal.gotchas: A trial flag on the org blocks every event's public forms, and a trial flag on any event behind an org Site form blocks that form. Check both flags. At ship time US had 3 trial orgs and 7 trial events, EU 1 trial event; confirm none is live and collecting.
internal.talk_track: While you set up on a trial, your forms are a safe preview: people can try them and save drafts, and submissions and payments open the moment your account is live.

entries.title: Large session lists load faster: subsessions load when you expand a parent
entries.summary: On **Program → Sessions** and the agenda's **List** tab, a parent session's subsessions now load when you expand it, with a short **Loading…** row, instead of arriving with every page. When you search, a parent that matches only through its subsessions shows just the matching ones, already expanded, as filters already did. Pages of events with thousands of subsessions load in a fraction of the time.

where.path: Program → Sessions; Program → Agenda → List

entries.use_case: A program team running an event with hundreds of subsessions under a few parents can page, search and filter the Sessions list quickly instead of waiting on, or timing out on, every subsession at once.

cs_action.note: Automatic. Came out of the 2026-11-04 prod-us outage (SB-11108): CES 2027 (205 parents, 6,226 subsessions) list pages were 2-12 MB and OOM-killed API tasks; customers saw "CORS Error: Unable to reach the API".

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with many subsessions reports a slow Sessions or agenda list, or a "CORS Error: Unable to reach the API" while paging it.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events with large numbers of subsessions (abstract-driven medical and scientific meetings, CES-style programs).
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Sessions → expand a parent session
internal.gotchas: Exports, reports and the calendar still carry every subsession; only the list grid loads them on expand. A parent loads its subsessions once per list load; editing a row refreshes that row only.
internal.talk_track: Big programs page instantly now; a session's subsessions load when you open it.

entries.title: Admin shells, Ask panel and tab strips now fit phones
entries.summary: On screens narrower than a tablet, the event, AI Mode and Awards admin sidebars collapse into a slide-out drawer opened by a **Menu** button; the button is hidden on pages that have no sidebar. The **Ask** panel expands to full-screen instead of squeezing into a sliver. Tab strips scroll horizontally rather than pushing the page wider, and header actions (**Search**, **Ask**, **View portal**) shrink to icon-only buttons with accessible labels.

where.path: Any event, Awards or AI Mode admin page on a phone-sized screen

entries.use_case: Organizers and reviewers who need to check or update event details from a phone can now navigate the full admin interface without horizontal scrolling or inaccessible sidebars. The Ask panel is also fully usable on a phone, so quick AI queries work on the go.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for all customers. No configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer mentions they struggle to use Sessionboard on a phone or tablet, or when a reviewer complains the mobile experience is broken.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers, especially those with reviewers or team members who access the platform from mobile devices.
internal.staff_path: Open any event or Awards admin page on a 375 px-wide device and tap the Menu button in the header.
internal.gotchas: Pages with no sidebar (e.g. full-screen editors, My Reviews) intentionally show no Menu button — this is correct behaviour, not a bug. Roughly 18 builder/editor routes still scroll horizontally; those are tracked separately.
internal.talk_track: The full Sessionboard admin — event pages, Awards, and the Ask panel — now works on a phone. The sidebar slides in as a drawer, tab strips scroll instead of breaking the layout, and the Ask AI panel goes full-screen so you can actually read the response.

draft.docs_gap: The sidebar guide should add a section describing the phone drawer behaviour (Menu button, named dialog, focus return) and note that the icon rail appears on tablets.
draft.why_use_it: The sidebar gives you fast access to every module in an event or organization without leaving the page you are on. On a phone, the sidebar slides in as a drawer so it does not compete with page content; on a tablet it collapses to an icon rail. Use it whenever you need to jump between Sessions, Contacts, Portals or any other module while away from a desktop.

entries.title: Admin pages fit phone screens without horizontal scrolling
entries.summary: Page headers, directory toolbars, tab bars, and wizard step rails across ~60 admin pages now reflow or scroll correctly on 375 px screens. **Page headers** wrap the title and action buttons instead of pushing actions off-screen; **directory toolbars** (contacts, submissions, applications, follow-up forms, file requests, portal forms) wrap and gain phone padding; **tab bars** scroll sideways rather than widening the page; and **wizard rails** (session form, review plan, request form builder, session settings) stack above the step content with a capped, scrollable height. Desktop layouts are unchanged.

where.path: All admin pages

entries.use_case: Organizers and reviewers who need to manage sessions, contacts, or submissions from a phone can now navigate and act on any admin page without content being cut off or requiring horizontal scrolling.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for all customers. No configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that admin pages are hard to use on a phone or tablet, or when onsite staff need to manage sessions or contacts from a mobile device.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer whose team manages events from mobile devices, particularly onsite coordinators and reviewers.
internal.staff_path: Any admin page at 375 px viewport width
internal.gotchas: Webinar-related pages (EventShell, Webinars plan/loop/model, New event form, LiteProgram, ChannelPeople, pulse, Brand) are not included in this pass and may still overflow on phones.
internal.talk_track: The admin interface now reflows cleanly on phones — page headers, toolbars, tab bars and wizard steps all fit a 375 px screen without horizontal scrolling, so your team can manage the event from wherever they are.

draft.docs_gap: The sidebar guide and general navigation articles should note that the admin interface is designed to be usable on phone-sized screens, and list which surfaces (webinar pages) are not yet optimised for mobile.

entries.title: Webinar event pages send attendees to the provider's registration page
entries.summary: When a webinar's registration is handled by the provider (Zoom, Goldcast, etc.), the public event page now shows a **Register on [Provider]** button that opens the provider's registration page in a new tab, instead of displaying the Sessionboard form. Before the webinar is published, the button reads **Registration opens soon**. The **Key Facts** block shows the format as **Online on [Provider]**. Webinars that register through Sessionboard, and all field events, are unchanged.

where.path: Public event page → Register block / Key Facts

entries.use_case: When an organizer runs a webinar on Zoom or Goldcast and wants attendees to register directly with the provider, the public event page now routes them there automatically — no manual workaround or custom link needed.

cs_action.note: Behaviour is automatic once the API (web-api #5108) is deployed alongside this front-end change. No configuration required from organizers.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their Zoom or Goldcast webinar event page was showing the Sessionboard registration form instead of sending people to the provider.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer running provider-hosted webinars (Zoom, Goldcast, etc.) whose public event page is live.
internal.staff_path: Public event page for a webinar with provider-side registration
internal.gotchas: This front-end change reads a field only sent by web-api #5108. Against an older API build the webinar field is absent and the page behaves exactly as before — both PRs must be deployed together for the change to take effect.
internal.talk_track: If your webinar registration lives on Zoom or Goldcast, the public event page now shows a 'Register on [Provider]' button that takes attendees straight there in a new tab. Before you publish the webinar, it shows 'Registration opens soon' so the page is never broken.

draft.docs_gap: The publish-and-sync guide should add a note explaining that when registration mode is set to the provider, the public event page automatically shows a provider-branded registration button and suppresses the Sessionboard form.
draft.why_use_it: Publishing a webinar from Sessionboard keeps your program data, speaker profiles and marketing in one place while letting attendees register on the platform that hosts the live event. The event page reflects the webinar's real registration destination — whether that is Sessionboard or the provider — so attendees always land in the right place without extra redirects or confusion.

entries.title: Webinar improvements: survey editor, recording upload, Advocacy open link, suggested speakers/sponsors, provider-aware form, and webinar page templates
entries.summary: Six connected improvements to the Webinars module ship together. **Pre-webinar survey**: the survey editor now supports adding, removing, reordering, and retyping questions (open-answer or choice), setting options, max picks, and required flags; answer counts warn before hiding responses. **Recording upload**: an uploaded Media video can be set as the webinar recording from the **After** tab, alongside provider-synced recordings. **Advocacy open link**: **Share cards › Copy Advocacy link** creates the attendee campaign if needed and turns on the open sign-up link in one click. **Suggested people**: the **Speakers** and **Sponsors** panels surface the org's most frequent speakers and sponsors from other events in the last three years, filtered to people not already on the webinar. **Provider-aware new-webinar form**: Q&A, polls, practice session, cloud recording, and approve-registrants options are enabled only when the connected provider supports them. **Webinar page templates**: webinar events get their own six page templates (Live webinar, Expert panel, Product demo, Online workshop, Series episode, Members' Q&A) in the site builder, separate from field-event templates.

where.path: Webinars → [webinar] → Audience / After / Promotion / Speakers / Sponsors / Configuration

entries.use_case: Webinar organizers can now build and iterate on pre-event surveys without losing stored responses, attach an uploaded recording the moment it is ready rather than waiting for provider sync, and surface likely speakers and sponsors from their own event history — reducing the manual work of setting up and following up on each webinar.

cs_action.note: All six improvements are default-on for any org with Webinars access. No flags to flip.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to collect pre-webinar questions from attendees, how to get a recording live before the provider syncs it, or how to find speakers for a new webinar without searching the full CRM.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer actively running webinars through Sessionboard, especially those using Zoom, Goldcast, GoTo Webinar, Webex, or Microsoft Teams.
internal.staff_path: Webinars → open any webinar → Audience (survey), After (recording upload), Promotion (Advocacy open link), Speakers / Sponsors (suggested people); New webinar form (provider options); Site builder → Pages (webinar templates)
internal.gotchas: Removed survey questions are soft-deleted so stored answers are preserved, but the editor shows answer counts to warn before hiding a question type. The Advocacy open link only turns on open_signup; a paused campaign stays paused. Webinar page templates are separate from field-event templates — an id from the wrong set falls back to the kind's default silently.
internal.talk_track: You can now build your pre-webinar survey right in Sessionboard and edit it safely after responses come in, upload your own recording the moment it is ready, find speakers from your org's history in one click, and copy an Advocacy open link without any manual campaign setup.

draft.docs_gap: The /webinars/audience guide should add a section on editing the pre-webinar survey after responses have been collected, including the answer-count warning. The /webinars/after guide should document uploading a Media video as the webinar recording. The /webinars/advocacy guide should document the Share cards › Copy Advocacy link button and its open-signup behaviour. The /webinars/overview or a new /webinars/speakers guide should cover the suggested-people panel. The /site/site-builder guide should note the six webinar-specific page templates.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's Webinars module connects your webinar platform — Zoom, Goldcast, GoTo Webinar, Webex or Microsoft Teams — to your speaker CRM, marketing tools and program site so every webinar is managed in one place. Use it to collect registrations, survey your audience before the event, track engagement and attendance, publish the recording, and distribute social content — without switching between your webinar tool and a separate spreadsheet or email tool. The module is designed for teams that run webinars regularly and need a repeatable, trackable workflow from planning through follow-up.

entries.title: Webinar hub: Overview checklist, survey editor, database suggestions, After tab, and accessibility improvements
entries.summary: The webinar **Overview** tab now shows a stage-by-stage **Checklist** (Invite · Fill · Prepare · Day · After) that replaces the old stage strip, with progress indicators, a **Now** marker, and one-click links to the relevant tab or section. The **People** tab gains three views — **Registrants**, **Pre-webinar survey**, and **Attendance** — plus a full **Survey editor** to add, remove, reorder, and configure questions with confirmations before hiding answers. The **Program** tab's **Speakers** and **Sponsors** tables show a **From your database** panel with topic-matched and frequently-used contacts for one-click adding. The **After** tab is reorganised into three groups — **The recording**, **Follow up**, and **Share and reuse** — with a jump bar, sample-data previews on every card, and a direct recording upload. Share cards now include a **Copy Advocacy link** button; email signatures gain **Copy signature** and **View / Copy HTML**. The public survey (Pulse quiz) meets WCAG 2.1 AA at all tested viewports.

where.path: Webinars → [any webinar] → Overview / People / Program / After

entries.use_case: Webinar organizers can now see exactly what still needs doing at each stage of a webinar's lifecycle from a single checklist, edit their pre-webinar survey questions without leaving Sessionboard, add speakers and sponsors from their existing contact database in one click, and find all post-event follow-up actions — recording, recaps, Dispatch, Advocacy — in one organised tab.

cs_action.note: All changes are default-on for any customer with Webinars access. No configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to keep track of webinar setup tasks, edit their pre-webinar survey, find speakers from their existing database, or organise post-event follow-up.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer actively running webinars through Sessionboard, especially those using Zoom, Goldcast, GoTo Webinar, Webex, or Microsoft Teams integrations.
internal.staff_path: Webinars → open any webinar → Overview, People, Program, or After tab
internal.gotchas: The survey save, Advocacy open link, recording link, suggested-people, and webinar-template routes require API PR #5108 to be in production. Until then, those specific buttons return an error toast; the rest of the UI is fully functional. Suggested people quietly falls back to topic matches only if the API is not yet deployed.
internal.talk_track: The webinar hub now walks you through every stage with a checklist that tells you exactly what is done, what is next, and what Sessionboard handles automatically. You can edit your pre-webinar survey questions in-product, add speakers from your existing contact database in one click, and find everything you need after the webinar — recording, recaps, Dispatch, Advocacy — in one organised tab.

draft.docs_gap: The /webinars/overview guide should document the new stage-by-stage Checklist card (tabs, Now marker, done/to-do/optional/automatic rows, Waiting on you channel approvals, and Handled for you disclosure). The /webinars/audience guide should cover the three People tab views and the Survey editor (add/remove/drag questions, type, required, options, confirmations). The /webinars/after guide should describe the three After-tab groups, the jump bar, sample-data previews, and direct recording upload. The /webinars/advocacy guide should note the Copy Advocacy link on share cards and the Copy signature / View HTML on email signatures.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard's webinar hub brings every stage of a webinar — planning, promotion, day-of logistics, and post-event follow-up — into a single place so organizers do not need to switch between tools or remember what comes next. The Overview checklist surfaces outstanding tasks by stage and links directly to the screen that completes them. The People tab lets you manage registrants, run a pre-webinar survey, and review attendance from one toolbar. The After tab collects recording publishing, personalised follow-up, and social distribution in one view so nothing falls through the cracks after the live event ends.

entries.title: Program Planner and Abstract Library in every gallery create flow, with Brand kit design controls
entries.summary: The gallery create wizard now lists **Program Planner** and **Abstract Library** as templates in every entry point — the first-run rail, the template picker, and the **Session Catalog** step — so both gallery types are always reachable. The **Design** tab gains a **Session details** section (detail fields, session codes, non-credit label, grouped filter) and a **Library** layout option for abstract libraries. Every brand field in the **Design** tab shows the value inherited from the org's Brand kit, labelled **From brand kit**; a **Use brand kit** control hands the field back to the kit (clearing the gallery's override). A **Brand kit** link in the **Theme** section and the wizard's **Brand** step opens the org kit page in a new tab. Gallery cards and Sites tiles reflect the effective brand automatically.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries

where.path: Publish → Sites → Galleries

entries.use_case: Organizers building a public-facing program browser or abstract archive can now start either gallery type from any create entry point without hunting for the right path. Brand kit inheritance means the gallery's colours, fonts and logo stay in sync with the org's kit automatically — no manual updates needed when the kit changes.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically for orgs with Content Galleries in Preview. No configuration needed beyond enabling the feature.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to publish a public program browser or abstract archive, or when they want their gallery to stay on-brand without manually updating design settings.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using or evaluating Content Galleries, especially those with an established Brand kit and events that have sessions or abstracts.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Sites → Galleries → New gallery (or first-run rail)
internal.gotchas: The event year picker previously showed 'NaN' — this is now fixed to show the correct year from date_from. Orgs without the Marketing module will be redirected to the org kit page (not the event marketing brand page) when clicking the Brand kit link. Marketing Sites (awards / event portal builder) do not yet read the Brand kit — that is separate work.
internal.talk_track: You can now create a Program Planner or Abstract Library from any starting point in the gallery create flow. The Design tab shows your Brand kit values by default — if you haven't customised a colour or font, it follows the kit automatically. When the kit changes, every untouched gallery updates on reload.

draft.docs_gap: The content-galleries guide should add a section covering the Session details design controls (detail fields, session codes, non-credit label, grouped filter), the Library layout option, and how Brand kit inheritance works in the Design tab — including the "From brand kit" label, the "Use brand kit" reset control, and the Brand kit link in the Theme section and wizard Brand step.
draft.why_use_it: Content Galleries let you publish a branded, browsable program or abstract archive directly from your session data — no separate website build required. A Program Planner gives attendees a filterable, searchable view of sessions, credits and speakers; an Abstract Library surfaces the scientific or educational content of your meeting in a format familiar to academic audiences. Because galleries read from your org's Brand kit, every published page reflects your official colours, fonts and logo without extra configuration.

entries.title: Abstract Library and Program Planner templates for public Sites
entries.summary: Two new gallery templates are available when creating a **Content Gallery**: **Abstract Library** and **Program Planner**. The **Abstract Library** displays numbered abstracts with authors, numbered affiliations, disclosures, credits, and "Presented in" links; when a meeting has sessions but no abstracts yet, the hub browses sessions instead of showing an empty page. The **Program Planner** shows a day-by-day schedule with session counts, opening sessions, and a **Register** link. Both templates inherit colours, fonts, and logos from the org **Brand kit** automatically, and individual overrides are supported.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries; then Publish → Sites → Galleries → Create gallery

where.path: Publish → Sites → Galleries

entries.use_case: Medical and scientific associations that publish abstract archives or program planners — like those currently using abstractsonline — can now host a fully branded, searchable abstract library or day-by-day program planner directly on their Sessionboard site, with session codes, credits, ticketed workshop fees, and author affiliations, without a third-party tool.

cs_action.note: Ideal for medical, scientific, and academic association customers who currently use abstractsonline or a similar archive tool. Proactively show this to any customer running a CFP with abstracts, credits, or disclosures.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to publish an abstract archive, a program book, or a public-facing planner on their site, or when they mention abstractsonline or a similar tool.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical societies, academic associations, and scientific conferences that collect abstracts with author affiliations, disclosures, and CME credits.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Sites → Galleries → Create gallery → Abstract Library or Program Planner
internal.gotchas: Content Galleries must be enabled via Early Access (Preview). The four galleries currently in production all belong to the internal CS org, so no customer pages change on release. Brand kit inheritance restyles any untouched gallery automatically once the API ships.
internal.talk_track: You can now publish a fully branded abstract library or program planner directly from Sessionboard — complete with numbered abstracts, author affiliations, disclosures, credits, session codes, and ticketed workshop fees — without exporting data or maintaining a separate archive site.

draft.docs_gap: The content-galleries guide should add a section describing the Abstract Library and Program Planner templates — including the abstract numbering scheme, author affiliations, disclosures, credits, session codes, ticketed workshop fee chip, the sessions-only fallback when no abstracts exist, and the day/session-count layout of the planner hub.
draft.why_use_it: Content Galleries let you publish a polished, public-facing view of your program — abstracts, sessions, posters, or a day-by-day planner — directly from your Sessionboard data, with no manual export or third-party archive tool. The gallery inherits your brand kit's colours, fonts, and logos automatically, so every page stays on brand. Use a gallery when you want attendees, authors, or the public to browse, search, and filter your content before, during, or after the event.

entries.title: Control brand kit inheritance field-by-field in the Site builder
entries.summary: The Site branding inspector now shows a **Follow the brand kit** switch and a **Brand kit** link that opens the kit driving the site. Under each branding field (landing logo, gradient, font, portal logo, portal font, primary colour, accent colour) a **From brand kit** label appears while the field uses the kit's value; once you override a field, a **Use brand kit** button lets you restore the kit's value for that field individually.

where.path: Awards → Sites → [site] → Site builder → Branding

entries.use_case: When an organizer wants their awards or event portal site to stay visually consistent with the organisation's brand kit, they can turn on **Follow the brand kit** and let the kit drive all design fields automatically — or override individual fields while keeping the rest kit-driven.

cs_action.note: The switch defaults to on for new sites and off for all existing sites, so no existing site changes appearance on deploy.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to keep their awards site on-brand, or when they notice the site builder does not reflect their brand kit colours or fonts.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who use Brand kits and have one or more Awards or event portal sites.
internal.staff_path: Awards → Sites → [site] → Site builder → Branding inspector
internal.gotchas: Existing sites have brand_kit_follow set to off by default — the site will not change until the organizer explicitly turns the switch on. The panel only renders when the API returns a brand_kit block (requires companion API PR #5110); against an older API the builder behaves exactly as before.
internal.talk_track: You can now connect your awards site directly to your Brand kit. Turn on Follow the brand kit and every logo, colour and font field pulls from the kit automatically. Override any individual field when you need a site-specific look, and use Use brand kit to snap it back.

draft.docs_gap: The site branding guide should add a section explaining the Follow the brand kit switch, the per-field From brand kit / Use brand kit labels, and the Brand kit shortcut link, including the default-off behaviour for existing sites.
draft.why_use_it: The Site builder's brand kit integration lets you connect your awards or event portal site to a central Brand kit so that logos, colours and fonts stay consistent without manual updates. Toggling **Follow the brand kit** on applies the kit's values across all branding fields at once, while per-field controls let you override specific elements when a site needs its own look. The canvas preview always reflects the kit's current values, so what you see in the builder matches what visitors see on the published site.

entries.title: New Marketing Sites automatically inherit the org's Brand kit
entries.summary: Any Marketing Site (awards or org portal) created after this release reads colours, heading font and logo directly from the org's **Brand kit** — no manual re-entry needed. Existing Sites are unchanged; authors can opt an older Site in from the site builder by toggling **Brand kit** in the site settings. A value the author sets in the builder always wins over the kit, and resetting it to the default hands control back to the kit. Cloned Sites carry the source's setting.

where.path: Awards → Sites → [Site] → Site builder → Settings

entries.use_case: Organizers who maintain a Brand kit no longer need to re-enter colours, fonts and logos when creating a new awards or org-portal Site — the Site picks them up automatically. For older Sites, a single toggle in the builder opts them in without touching any values the author already set.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically. New Sites follow the kit by default; existing Sites are untouched until an author opts in.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why their new awards site doesn't match their brand, or when they want to keep Sites consistent with event pages without manual styling.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who have a Brand kit configured and create new awards or org-portal Sites.
internal.staff_path: Awards → Sites → [Site] → Site builder → Settings → Brand kit toggle
internal.gotchas: Only new Sites follow the kit by default — every existing Site has brand_kit_follow=false and will not change appearance until the author explicitly opts in. The kit's text colour is never inherited. Icon fonts and self-hosted fonts in the kit are skipped (the Site loads fonts from Google Fonts). The accent colour #1A5ADB is treated as 'never picked' and will be overridden by the kit.
internal.talk_track: Any new awards or portal Site you create now starts from your Brand kit automatically — colours, heading font and logo are all pulled in. If you want an older Site to match, there's a single toggle in the site builder settings to opt it in without losing any styling you've already set.

draft.docs_gap: The site branding section of the guide should document the new Brand kit follow behaviour: that new Sites inherit kit colours, heading font and logo by default; how to opt an existing Site in via the builder toggle; that author-set values always override the kit; and the limitations (text colour, icon fonts and self-hosted fonts are not inherited).
draft.why_use_it: Brand kits let you define your organisation's logo, colours and heading font in one place so every surface that reads from the kit stays visually consistent. When you update the kit, every new Site that follows it reflects the change automatically — without reopening the builder. Use this whenever you want awards sites and org portals to match your event pages and content galleries out of the box.

entries.title: Two new gallery templates — Program Planner and Abstract Library — plus automatic Brand kit inheritance
entries.summary: Two new **Content Gallery** templates are now available when creating a gallery: **Program Planner** (event-scoped, shows sessions with credits, ticketed workshops, session codes, disclosures and forthcoming flags) and **Abstract Library** (org-wide, spans multiple years of meetings and surfaces presentations/abstracts as browsable items). Both templates include a guided checklist and built-in kind filter. Additionally, any gallery whose design fields have not been manually set now automatically inherits the org's **Brand kit** primary colour, accent colour, heading font and logo; the **Design** tab shows each inherited value labelled **From brand kit** alongside a **Brand kit** link, and setting a value overrides the kit while clearing it hands control back.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Content Galleries

where.path: Publish → Sites → Galleries → New Gallery

entries.use_case: Medical and scientific associations can now publish a branded, filterable Program Planner for a single meeting — complete with CME credits, ticketed workshops and session codes — and a multi-year Abstract Library that lets attendees browse presentations across every past meeting, all without custom development.

cs_action.note: Medical and scientific customers (ASA and similar) are the primary target; proactively show them the Program Planner and Abstract Library templates. Brand kit inheritance is automatic for all galleries in preview — no action needed, but worth flagging to customers who previously complained about off-brand defaults.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When talking to medical, scientific or academic associations that run multi-year abstract archives or credit-bearing meetings, or when any customer asks how to keep their gallery on brand.
internal.who_should_get_it: Medical/scientific associations with CME credits, ticketed workshops or multi-year abstract archives; any customer using Content Galleries who has a Brand kit configured.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Sites → Galleries → New Gallery (select Program Planner or Abstract Library); Design tab shows Brand kit values
internal.gotchas: Abstract Library is org-wide and can only be created at the org level — event-only staff receive a 403. Brand kit text colour is intentionally never applied to galleries (only primary, accent, font and logo inherit). The light logo variant only activates on a dark canvas theme. Marketing Sites (awards / event portal builder) do not yet read the Brand kit — that is separate work.
internal.talk_track: You can now create a Program Planner gallery that shows your full meeting agenda with credits, ticketed workshops and session codes, and an Abstract Library that spans every year of your conference — both automatically styled from your Brand kit so they look right from day one.

draft.docs_gap: The content-galleries guide should add a section describing the Program Planner and Abstract Library templates (their checklist steps, data sources, presentation/abstract item type, and org-wide vs event scope), and a section explaining Brand kit inheritance on the Design tab (which columns follow the kit, how the "From brand kit" label and Brand kit link work, and how to override or reset individual values).
draft.why_use_it: Content Galleries let you publish a polished, public-facing browsing experience for your sessions, presentations and abstracts without building a custom website. Use a Program Planner to give attendees a filterable view of your meeting's full agenda — including credits, ticketed workshops and session codes — and an Abstract Library to make years of scientific content discoverable in one place. Brand kit inheritance means every new gallery opens on-brand automatically, and any design value you set in the gallery takes precedence over the kit so you retain full control.

entries.title: Add an Events list block to marketing Sites that auto-populates from live field events and webinars
entries.summary: A new **Events list** block is available on marketing Site landing pages and custom pages. Add it to a Site and it automatically pulls the organization's published field events and/or webinars — with name, date, location, registration status and a CTA link — resolved fresh on every public page load. No manual link maintenance required; events appear or disappear as they are published, unpublished or ended.

where.path: Sites → Site builder → Landing page or custom page → Add block → Events list

entries.use_case: Organizers who run multiple field events or webinars under one organization can add a single **Events list** block to their marketing Site and let it stay current automatically — visitors always see the live lineup with accurate dates, locations and registration status without anyone editing the Site each time an event is added or ends.

cs_action.note: The block is available in the Site builder once the API is deployed. The builder UI entry is gated on the block catalog listing events_list (requiresServerKind), so the block only appears after this API release is live.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to keep a public events page current without editing it manually after every change, or when they are building a marketing site for an org that runs recurring field events or webinars.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers who manage multiple field events or webinars under one org and publish a marketing or program site.
internal.staff_path: Sites → Site builder → Landing page or custom page → Add block → Events list
internal.gotchas: The block only lists events whose event-page Site is published. Draft events, archived events, invite-only events and events without a published event page are excluded. Setting a seriesId filter lists nothing until the Series feature ships (no table exists yet). The builder preview endpoint is public by design — it only surfaces events already visible at /e/<slug>. Orgs on the gatherings_registration feature flag get richer capacity/waitlist data; others fall back to kind_settings.
internal.talk_track: Instead of hand-building a list of event links that goes stale, add the Events list block to your Site and it pulls your live field events and webinars automatically — dates, locations, registration status and CTA buttons update on every page load with no Site edits needed.

draft.docs_gap: The setting-up-your-sessionboard-site guide should add a section documenting the Events list block: its configuration options (source, seriesId, showPast, layout, ctaLabel, heading, intro), how events qualify to appear, what each item displays (name, date, city, status, CTA), and how status values (open, waitlist, full, closed) are determined.
draft.why_use_it: The Site builder lets you publish a branded marketing site for your organization or program without writing code. Blocks like **Events list** pull live data from your Sessionboard records so the page stays accurate as your event calendar evolves. Use it when you want a public-facing hub that reflects your current schedule, registration availability and event details without manual updates.

entries.title: Connect Webex Webinars as a webinar provider
entries.summary: **Webex Webinars** is now available as a webinar provider alongside Zoom, Goldcast and ON24. Organizers can connect a Webex account via OAuth from **Apps → Webex Webinars**, start or import webinars using Webex, and read ratings and feedback from Webex's built-in webinar survey in the **Engagement** report. The **Webex Webinars** app card appears in the **Webinars** category of the App Marketplace once the platform has activated the integration.

enable.path: Apps → Webex Webinars → Connect with Webex

where.path: Apps → Webex Webinars; Webinars → Start / Import / Settings

entries.use_case: For teams that run webinars on Webex, this lets them manage the full webinar lifecycle — planning, publishing, syncing and post-event engagement — inside Sessionboard without switching between tools. Ratings and feedback from Webex's native survey flow directly into the Engagement report.

cs_action.note: The app card only renders once the API-side release (web-api#5033) is also deployed and the server catalog lists 'webex'. Confirm both sides are live before telling customers it is available.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks whether Sessionboard supports Webex, or when they are evaluating webinar platform options alongside Zoom, Goldcast and ON24.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer who runs webinars on Webex Webinars and wants to manage them from Sessionboard.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Webex Webinars (visible once the API catalog includes 'webex')
internal.gotchas: The UI is gated on the API listing 'webex' in offeredProviders — if the API side has not shipped yet, the card and provider options will not appear even though the UI code is deployed. An event already configured on Webex will continue to show Webex regardless of the API gate.
internal.talk_track: You can now connect your Webex account directly in Sessionboard — start or import webinars, keep speaker and session data in sync, and pull ratings and feedback from Webex's survey straight into your Engagement report, all without leaving the platform.

draft.docs_gap: The /apps/webex-webinars-integration guide should document the OAuth connection flow, what data syncs (sessions, speakers, recordings, engagement/ratings), how the sign-in expired / Reconnect panel works, and how to import past Webex webinars — mirroring the structure of the Zoom and ON24 guides.
draft.why_use_it: The Webex Webinars integration connects your Webex account to Sessionboard so you can start, manage and import webinars without leaving the platform. Speaker details, session metadata and engagement data — including ratings and feedback from Webex's built-in survey — sync automatically, giving you a single place to run your webinar programme regardless of which platform hosts the live event.

entries.title: Duplicate keeps every participant in their role and order
entries.summary: Duplicating a session copies every participant into the same role and order as the original, with their affiliations and role answers. That includes custom roles and built-in roles an event renamed or moved to another role type, such as a **Chairperson** role renamed "Coauthor" that counts as a speaker. Previously those participants landed in the first speaker role, and the order across roles could change.

where.path: Sessions → [session] → Duplicate

entries.use_case: When an organizer duplicates a session that has a custom or re-cored role (for example, a Chairperson role renamed to "Coauthor"), the copy now reflects the exact roster — right roles, right order — so no manual reassignment is needed after duplication.

cs_action.note: Ships automatically. No configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that duplicating a session scrambles participant roles or drops participants — especially events that have renamed or re-cored a system role like Chairperson.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Duplicate Session with custom or re-cored participant roles, or with Sessions 2.0 enabled.
internal.staff_path: Sessions → open any session → Duplicate
internal.gotchas: The bug was confirmed in production on events that re-cored the system 'chairperson' slug to a custom label (e.g. 'Coauthor' with core role 'speaker'). Events using only the default Presenter/Chair/Moderator roles without re-coring were also affected by incorrect ordering. The abstract-to-session conversion path shares the same fix.
internal.talk_track: Duplicating a session now copies every participant into their correct role and in the same order as the original — including any custom or renamed roles — so the copy is ready to use without manual cleanup.

draft.docs_gap: The clone-a-session guide should note that custom and re-cored system roles, participant order across roles, role-attribute answers, affiliations, and legacy-only seats are all preserved in the duplicate.

entries.title: Marketing module: error states, safer sends, smarter polls, and accessibility fixes
entries.summary: Across Dispatch, Advocacy, Clips, Quotes, Media, Create and Market, load failures now show an error card with a **Retry** button instead of an empty list or endless skeleton. In Dispatch, **Send now** asks for confirmation before sending, **Send test**, **Duplicate** and **Nudge** buttons disable and spin while running to prevent double-sends, and deleting a body-of-work item requires confirmation. Media Discover's background scan stops automatically 10 minutes after the newest import (or on error) instead of polling forever. Quotes shows the real total count, Market overview shows "—" while numbers load and "100+" at the cap, and search on Dispatches, Clips and Advocacy campaigns now matches accented characters. A **Draft** tab has been added to Dispatches. Icon-only buttons in Dispatch, Media and Advocacy now carry accessible labels.

where.path: Marketing → Dispatch / Advocacy / Clips / Quotes / Media / Create / Market

entries.use_case: Organizers running post-event content distribution can now recover from load failures without refreshing the page, confirm before sending a Dispatch to their full recipient list, and trust that background scans won't run indefinitely if an import stalls.

cs_action.note: All changes are default-on frontend fixes; no configuration required.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports blank screens or empty lists in Marketing, accidental double-sends on Dispatch, or confusion about why Media Discover kept scanning.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer actively using the Marketing module (Dispatch, Advocacy, Clips, Quotes, Media, Create or Market).
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Dispatch / Advocacy / Clips / Quotes / Media / Create / Market
internal.gotchas: The 'Send now' confirmation dialog is new — customers who relied on a single click to send immediately will now see an extra step. MediaAttributionEditor still shows contact/account IDs instead of names (API limitation, noted as left for later).
internal.talk_track: Load errors in Marketing now show a Retry button so you never mistake a network hiccup for an empty library. Dispatch also asks you to confirm before sending to your full list, and buttons disable while a send is in flight so you can't accidentally send twice.

draft.docs_gap: The Dispatch guide should document the new Send now confirmation dialog, the Draft tab, and the per-button pending/disabled states for Send test, Duplicate and Nudge. The Media library guide should note that the Discover scan stops automatically after 10 minutes of inactivity or on error.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing brings together Dispatch, Advocacy, Clips, Quotes, Media and Create so your team can produce and distribute event content from one place. Use it to send personalised social share kits to speakers, schedule email dispatches to your audience, clip and quote recordings, and track how content spreads — all without switching between tools.

entries.title: Resolve DKIM selector conflicts when setting up a custom sending domain
entries.summary: When setting up an email sending domain, step 2 now shows a live DNS status per record — **Found**, **Not added yet**, or **In use by SendGrid** (hover to see the current value). If the default `s1._domainkey` / `s2._domainkey` selectors are already claimed by another SendGrid account, a **Clash notice** lists each conflicting name, explains why it should not be changed, and suggests free alternatives (e.g. `sb._domainkey` + `sb2._domainkey`). Click **Use alternate records** to apply them in one step, or **Choose my own names** to enter custom selectors. An **Advanced settings** section on the setup form and under the records panel exposes **Use a custom DKIM selector** and **Use a custom return path** checkboxes, each with a live preview of the resulting record names.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable the custom email domain add-on; then Settings → Domains → Email domain

where.path: Settings → Domains → Email domain

entries.use_case: Organizations whose DNS already has `s1._domainkey` / `s2._domainkey` pointing at a different SendGrid account — such as a corporate email platform — can now complete sending-domain setup without filing a support ticket: the clash is detected automatically, free selector names are suggested, and the new records are created in one click.

cs_action.note: Proactively contact customers who previously got stuck on domain verification because of a DKIM selector clash — they can now complete setup themselves without a staff-side card.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that their sending domain is stuck on 'Not found' or that they cannot add the DKIM records because their IT team says the names are already in use.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers at large organisations (associations, universities, enterprises) that run their own SendGrid account for transactional or marketing email alongside Sessionboard.
internal.staff_path: Settings → Domains → Email domain → step 2 (DNS records panel)
internal.gotchas: Requires web-api PR #5112 to be deployed first; until then the DNS-check endpoint returns 404 and customers see the old panel with no alternate-record controls. Replacing records on an already-verified domain remains staff-only.
internal.talk_track: If your IT team already uses SendGrid and the default DKIM selector names are taken, Sessionboard now detects the clash, suggests free names, and lets you switch to them in one click — no support ticket needed.

draft.docs_gap: The /settings/domains guide should add a section explaining DKIM selector conflicts — what causes them, how the In use by SendGrid status appears, and how to use the Clash notice to apply alternate selectors or enter custom names via Advanced settings.
draft.why_use_it: Sending email from your own domain improves deliverability and keeps your brand in the From address instead of a shared Sessionboard address. The Domains setup walks you through adding the required DNS records and confirms each one is live before activating the domain. Use it whenever you want speaker invitations, portal emails and campaigns to arrive from an address your attendees recognise and trust.

entries.title: Custom sending domain DNS check no longer flags wildcard records as conflicts
entries.summary: The DNS authentication check for custom sending domains now ignores wildcard DNS records when deciding whether a required CNAME or MX record is already taken. Previously, organisations whose domain published a wildcard MX or CNAME (e.g. `*.example.org`) would see every suggested return-path subdomain reported as a **conflict**, prompting an endless regeneration loop. The check now probes for a wildcard answer and treats a matching result as a free slot, so the **Domain** setup page shows the correct **Missing** status and lets setup proceed normally.

where.path: Settings → Domains → Email domain → DNS authentication status

entries.use_case: Organisations whose domain uses a wildcard DNS record (common in large associations and enterprises) can now complete custom sending-domain setup without being incorrectly told their return-path subdomain is already in use.

cs_action.note: Any customer with the custom sending domain add-on who reported a persistent 'conflict' on their return-path or CNAME records — especially large associations or enterprise accounts — should be re-checked; the fix is now live and they can retry DNS verification.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer with the Email Domain add-on says their DNS check always shows a conflict even after they've added the required records, or when they keep regenerating their return-path subdomain without success.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the custom sending domain add-on whose parent domain publishes a wildcard MX or CNAME record — common in large associations and enterprise IT environments.
internal.staff_path: Settings → Domains → Email domain → check DNS status
internal.gotchas: The fix correctly scopes wildcard detection per parent domain, so a real DKIM conflict (e.g. an existing SendGrid selector) still surfaces as a conflict — only genuine wildcard matches are suppressed.
internal.talk_track: If your domain uses a wildcard DNS record, the sending-domain setup page was incorrectly flagging your return-path subdomain as already taken. That's fixed — the check now recognises wildcard records and correctly shows those slots as available.

draft.docs_gap: The custom email domain guide should note that domains with wildcard DNS records (e.g. *.example.org) are supported, and explain that the DNS check automatically distinguishes wildcard matches from real record conflicts.

entries.title: Dispatch shows clear not-found and no-access messages instead of a retry loop
entries.summary: Opening a deleted or inaccessible Dispatch now shows a specific message — **"Dispatch not found"** for a 404 or **"You don't have access to this dispatch"** for a 403 — instead of retrying three times and displaying a generic connection-error card. Long dispatch names on list cards are now truncated so the status badge and action menu stay visible, and on the detail page the action buttons wrap below the title on narrow screens rather than being squeezed off-screen.

where.path: Marketing → Dispatch

entries.use_case: When a team member follows a stale link to a deleted dispatch, or lacks permission to view one, they immediately see a clear explanation rather than a confusing connection-error message — reducing support requests and confusion during campaign handoffs.

cs_action.note: Behaviour fix ships automatically for all Dispatch beta customers. No configuration needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: If a customer reports seeing a 'check your connection' error on a dispatch that no longer exists, or complains that the status badge is hidden on cards with long names.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Dispatch (beta).
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Dispatch → open any dispatch card or detail page
internal.gotchas: The 403 and 404 messages are translated into German, Spanish and French; English is the fallback for any other locale.
internal.talk_track: Deleted or restricted dispatches now show a clear explanation right away instead of spinning through retries and showing a misleading network-error message.

draft.docs_gap: The Dispatch guide should note that navigating to a deleted or inaccessible dispatch shows a specific error message rather than a generic retry prompt.

entries.title: Questions on each credit type, and certificates with your signatory and accreditation statement
entries.summary: Each **credit type** can now ask its own questions (Yes / No, short or paragraph answers, one or several choices, a 1–5 rating, an acknowledgement), required or optional, on **every claim** or **once per attendee**, and copy them to other types. The claim site asks them before saving a claim, and **Responses** shows the answers. The rebuilt **Credit types** settings also set each type's certificate template, **signatory name and title** and **accreditation statement**.

enable.path: Event → Early Access → Credit Claiming → Request access (CS turns it on; organization-wide card for field events)

where.path: Program → Configure → Settings → Credit types

entries.use_case: Accrediting bodies each want their own attestation and wording. Put the questions and the certificate statement on the credential itself, and every attendee who claims it answers them and gets a certificate your accreditor accepts, without a separate form or a manual merge.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a CME, nursing or pharmacy customer collects attestations or accreditor questions in a separate form, or asks for their signatory and accreditation statement on certificates.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on the Credit Claiming beta with accredited sessions, especially medical and scientific societies.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → Configure → Settings → Credit types → open a type → Questions / Certificate
internal.gotchas: Credit types are organization-wide: changing questions or wording changes them for every event. These questions are not Surveys; the session feedback survey is separate. The Attend app cannot ask them: it refuses those claims and sends the attendee to the claim site.
internal.talk_track: Put each accreditor's questions and certificate wording on the credit type once; attendees answer them when they claim, and you read the answers under Responses or export them.

entries.title: A branded, multilingual claim site with My certificates and scoped transcripts
entries.summary: The attendee claim site now carries the event's logo, name, dates and brand colour, works on a phone, and switches between English, German, Spanish and French (it starts in the browser's language). Signed-in attendees get **Claim credits**, **My certificates** and **Transcript** tabs. **My certificates** lists one certificate per credit with **View** and **PDF**, plus **Download all** and a **Summary certificate** per credit type, and the transcript can be limited to one credit type or one credit. Certificates are redesigned with the certificate number, issue date, session code, signatory and statement.

enable.path: Event → Early Access → Credit Claiming → Request access (CS turns it on; organization-wide card for field events)

where.path: The claim site (Copy claim link on Program → After the event → Credit Claiming)

entries.use_case: Attendees get a claim site that looks like the customer's event, in their language, and can pull exactly the certificate or transcript a licensing board asks for without emailing the organizer.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer sends attendees to the claim site, has international attendees, or fields support emails asking for certificates or a per-credential transcript.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event on the Credit Claiming beta.
internal.staff_path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming → Open claim site
internal.gotchas: Branding comes from the event's brand kit, falling back to the event logo and highlight colour. The language choice is stored per browser.
internal.talk_track: The claim site now looks like your event and speaks your attendees' language; they download every certificate, a summary certificate per credential, or a transcript for just one credential.

entries.title: Credit Claiming admin: filters on every tab, Claimants audit, richer report and exports
entries.summary: **Program → After the event → Credit Claiming** is rebuilt with six tabs: **Claims**, **Credits per session**, **Attendance**, **Audit**, **Report** and **Activity**. Filter by credit type, session, attendance source, flagged claims, claim date and attendee. **Audit** gains a **Claimants** view (everyone who claimed a credit type), **Report** breaks claims down by credit type, session and day, **Attendance** lists verified attendance and who has not claimed yet, and every tab has **Export** to CSV or Excel as a background export under **History → Exports**. The header links to the claiming settings, credit types, the claim link and the claim site, and the claiming settings are regrouped into Access, Claim window (with presets), Session list, Rules and Attendee instructions.

enable.path: Event → Early Access → Credit Claiming → Request access (CS turns it on; organization-wide card for field events)

where.path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming

entries.use_case: The audit and report an accrediting body asks for come straight off the page: filter to one credential or one session, list every claimant, and export exactly what is on screen instead of rebuilding it in a spreadsheet.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer prepares the post-event accreditation report or asks who claimed a credential, which claims lack attendance, or who attended but has not claimed.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event on the Credit Claiming beta.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → After the event → Credit Claiming
internal.gotchas: Exports run as background jobs and land under History → Exports. Attendance labels in the admin read Swapcard scan / Imported / Check-in / Self-reported; the attendee transcript still says Session scan / Imported attendance / Check-in. The Eval claim requirement is now labelled Survey.
internal.talk_track: Filter to what your accreditor asks for, switch the audit to claimants, and export that exact view to Excel.

entries.title: Credit Claiming activity log
entries.summary: A new **Activity** tab on the Credit Claiming page logs attendee sign-ins, claims, removed claims and certificate and transcript downloads, and every staff grant, reversal, attendance import, credit change, settings change, credit type change and export, with who did it and when. Filter by who, action, text and date, and export it. The same entries appear in **History** under **Credit claim**.

enable.path: Event → Early Access → Credit Claiming → Request access (CS turns it on; organization-wide card for field events)

where.path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming → Activity; History → Credit claim

entries.use_case: When an attendee disputes a claim or an auditor asks who changed a credit, the answer is one filter away instead of a support ticket.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer is audited by an accrediting body, or needs to resolve an attendee saying a claim disappeared.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every event on the Credit Claiming beta.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → After the event → Credit Claiming → Activity
internal.gotchas: The log is not available to users whose Credits access is limited to some portfolios (the tab shows Could not load activity). Attendance-import History rows now sit under the Credit claim subject rather than the event.
internal.talk_track: Every sign-in, claim, download and staff change is logged, filterable and exportable.

entries.title: Credit Claiming Manager and Credit Claiming Viewer roles
entries.summary: Credit Claiming has its own permissions in **Event Team → Permissions** (**Can view claims, attendance, audit and reports** and **Can manage credit claiming**), and two new default roles at event and organization level: **Credit Claiming Manager** runs credit claiming and **Credit Claiming Viewer** sees it read-only, with nothing else in the event. Someone with only these permissions gets a short sidebar and lands on the Credit Claiming page.

enable.path: Event → Early Access → Credit Claiming → Request access (CS turns it on; organization-wide card for field events)

where.path: Event Team → Permissions → Credit Claiming; Organization Settings → Team → Permissions

entries.use_case: Give an accrediting partner or a CE coordinator exactly the claims, audit, reports and exports they need, without opening the rest of the event to them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants an association partner, accreditor or CE vendor to see or manage claims, or asks how to lock someone to just credit claiming.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Credit Claiming beta that work with partner associations or outside CE staff.
internal.staff_path: Event → Event Team → Permissions → Credit Claiming Manager / Credit Claiming Viewer
internal.gotchas: Defaults: Admin User and Admin Lite get view + manage, Reporting Only Admin gets view, every other role (including custom roles) gets neither until turned on. The stock roles are not editable; duplicate them. The roles appear only on events/orgs that run Credit Claiming.
internal.talk_track: Invite your partner as a Credit Claiming Viewer: they see claims, the audit and reports, and nothing else.

entries.title: Credit Claiming reports, dashboard and live share link
entries.summary: Credit Claiming is now in **Insights**. An **Insights** menu on the Credit Claiming page creates or opens a **Credit Claiming** dashboard (claims and claimants, credit by type, claims per day, most-claimed sessions), opens the nine **Credits** reports (by credit type, claimants, by session, by day, claims without verified attendance, attendee totals, sessions offering each type, all claims, attendance by source), and shares the dashboard as a live read-only link. The Credits widgets are in the dashboard widget catalog too.

enable.path: Event → Early Access → Credit Claiming → Request access (CS turns it on; organization-wide card for field events)

where.path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming → Insights; Reports; event dashboards

entries.use_case: Send leadership or an accrediting partner a live Credit Claiming dashboard instead of a spreadsheet that is stale the moment it is attached.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports CE numbers to leadership or a partner association, or builds dashboards for an accredited event.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Credit Claiming beta whose users have Insights access.
internal.staff_path: Event → Program → After the event → Credit Claiming → Insights
internal.gotchas: The Insights menu shows only on events running Credit Claiming and for roles with Insights access. CreditClaim in SbQL now hides reversal rows, so Learning report counts can drop slightly for existing customers.
internal.talk_track: One click builds the Credit Claiming dashboard, and Share live report gives your partner a read-only link that stays current.

entries.title: The sending domain records show your DMARC record
entries.summary: The DNS records under **Settings > Domains → Email domain** now include an optional **DMARC** row: **Found** with the policy in effect (including one inherited from a parent domain), **More than one record** when the domain publishes two, or **Not set** with a suggested `v=DMARC1; p=none;` record to copy. It is informational and does not affect verification.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Custom Sending Domain; then Settings > Domains

where.path: Settings > Domains → Email domain → DNS records

entries.use_case: Gmail and Yahoo require DMARC for bulk senders. The setup now shows whether the domain has a DMARC policy and hands the customer a safe starter record, so a deliverability gap is caught before the first big send.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer sets up a sending domain or reports deliverability problems with Gmail or Yahoo.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Custom Sending Domain.
internal.staff_path: Settings > Domains → Email domain → Show the DNS records
internal.gotchas: The row is optional and not counted in the records to add or in the IT hand-off. On a verified domain it appears once the DNS records are opened. Two DMARC records at one name show More than one record.
internal.talk_track: The domain setup now shows your DMARC record and gives you a starter record if you have none.
